# `m.futures.market_status`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Whether each futures product is trading right now.

```python
m.futures.market_status(*, product_code=None, limit=None)
```

[All datasets](README.md)

|  |  |
| --- | --- |
| Methods | `fetch()`, `poll()` |
| Served by | REST |
| `poll()` | `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`: holds exactly the latest cycle's rows, keyed by `ProductCode` and `TradingVenue`; `mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND` also keys by `Timestamp` |

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `product_code` | Only this product, such as `"ES"`, or these, such as `["ES", "NQ"]`. A table of them in a `ProductCode` column works too. Leave it out for every product. |  |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. A table of product codes caps every code's requests instead. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `timestamp`: "The timestamp for the given market event." | REST |
| `MarketEvent` | String | The current status of the market for the product. | REST |
| `Name` | String | The name of the futures product. | REST |
| `ProductCode` | String | The product code of the futures contracts for which you want statuses. | REST |
| `SessionEndDate` | String | The trading date for the current session. | REST |
| `TradingVenue` | String | The trading venue (MIC) for the exchange on which the corresponding product trades. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
